The application-side census is [`blast-radius-analyzer`](../../blast-radius-analyzer/SKILL.md)'s (checklist: SKILL.md lines 55–64 and 73 — FKs, indexes, views, triggers; then migrations, seeders, reports) and is **not** restated here; this file adds only what that one cannot see — the catalog.

Run it **before** any drop, rename or type change, before the migration plan is
written. Every query is a read-only `SELECT`.

Confidence marks: **H** — the catalog table and every column named are on the
cited page. **M** — the table is right, but the result needs interpretation
(text search, prefix logic).

## 1. Foreign-key graph, into and out of a table

### PostgreSQL — `pg_constraint` (H)

Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/catalog-pg-constraint.html

```sql
-- out of public.orders (orders references others) and into it (others reference orders)
SELECT c.conname, c.conrelid::regclass AS child_table,
       c.confrelid::regclass AS parent_table, pg_get_constraintdef(c.oid) AS definition
FROM pg_constraint c
WHERE c.contype = 'f'
  AND 'public.orders'::regclass IN (c.conrelid, c.confrelid)
ORDER BY parent_table, child_table, c.conname;
```

`pg_get_constraintdef` renders the column list and the `ON DELETE` / `ON UPDATE`
actions, so the referential action is read from the same row
(https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/functions-info.html).

### MySQL / MariaDB — `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` + `REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS` (H)

Sources: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/information-schema-key-column-usage-table.html ·
https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/information-schema-referential-constraints-table.html

```sql
SELECT k.CONSTRAINT_NAME, k.TABLE_NAME AS child_table, k.COLUMN_NAME AS child_column,
       k.REFERENCED_TABLE_NAME AS parent_table, k.REFERENCED_COLUMN_NAME AS parent_column,
       r.UPDATE_RULE, r.DELETE_RULE
FROM information_schema.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE k
JOIN information_schema.REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS r
  ON r.CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA = k.CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA
 AND r.CONSTRAINT_NAME   = k.CONSTRAINT_NAME
WHERE k.TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE()
  AND k.REFERENCED_TABLE_NAME IS NOT NULL
  AND (k.TABLE_NAME = 'orders' OR k.REFERENCED_TABLE_NAME = 'orders')
ORDER BY parent_table, child_table, k.ORDINAL_POSITION;
```

The MySQL 8.4 pages are the cited source; on MariaDB, confirm the same columns
against the server's own `information_schema` before relying on the output.

## 2. Views, triggers and routines that depend on an object

### PostgreSQL — views via `pg_depend` → `pg_rewrite` (H)

A view's dependency on a column is recorded in `pg_depend` against the view's
rewrite rule, not the view itself; `pg_rewrite.ev_class` leads back to the view.
`refobjsubid` is the column number.
Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/catalog-pg-depend.html ·
https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/catalog-pg-rewrite.html

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT v.oid::regclass AS dependent_view, v.relkind, a.attname AS column_used
FROM pg_depend d
JOIN pg_rewrite   r ON r.oid = d.objid
JOIN pg_class     v ON v.oid = r.ev_class
JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = d.refobjid AND a.attnum = d.refobjsubid
WHERE d.classid    = 'pg_rewrite'::regclass
  AND d.refclassid = 'pg_class'::regclass
  AND d.refobjid   = 'public.orders'::regclass
  AND a.attname    = 'legacy_ref'          -- drop the filter to list every column used
  AND v.oid <> d.refobjid;                 -- exclude the table's own rules
```

`relkind` `v` is a view, `m` a materialized view. A view on a view is second
order: re-run with it as `refobjid`, then stop.

### PostgreSQL — triggers via `pg_trigger` (H)

Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/catalog-pg-trigger.html

```sql
SELECT t.tgname, t.tgfoid::regproc AS trigger_function, pg_get_triggerdef(t.oid)
FROM pg_trigger t
WHERE t.tgrelid = 'public.orders'::regclass
  AND NOT t.tgisinternal;                  -- internal triggers implement FKs, listed in § 1
```

### PostgreSQL — functions and procedures (M)

`pg_depend` only records a function body's dependencies when it uses the
SQL-standard body (`RETURN …` / `BEGIN ATOMIC … END`); the string-literal form
(`AS '…'`, which covers every PL/pgSQL function) "may leave dangling functions"
(https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createfunction.html). So run both:

```sql
-- tracked: SQL-standard bodies
SELECT DISTINCT d.objid::regprocedure AS dependent_routine
FROM pg_depend d
WHERE d.classid = 'pg_proc'::regclass AND d.refclassid = 'pg_class'::regclass
  AND d.refobjid = 'public.orders'::regclass;

-- untracked: text search over string bodies — matches are candidates, not proof
SELECT p.oid::regprocedure AS candidate_routine
FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace
WHERE n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema') AND p.prosrc ILIKE '%legacy_ref%';
```

Source for `prosrc`: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/catalog-pg-proc.html

### MySQL / MariaDB — views (M)

MySQL keeps **no column-level dependency catalog for views**.
`VIEW_TABLE_USAGE` lists, per view, the tables and views its definition uses —
table granularity only, no column
(https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/information-schema-view-table-usage-table.html).
Column use is read from the definition text in `VIEWS.VIEW_DEFINITION`
(https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/information-schema-views-table.html):

```sql
-- views that use the table (table-level, from the catalog)
SELECT VIEW_NAME FROM information_schema.VIEW_TABLE_USAGE
WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE() AND TABLE_NAME = 'orders';

-- views whose text names the column (column-level, by text search)
SELECT TABLE_NAME AS view_name
FROM information_schema.VIEWS
WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE()
  AND VIEW_DEFINITION LIKE '%legacy_ref%';
```

Each text hit is a candidate; read the definition. `VIEW_TABLE_USAGE` is not
verified on MariaDB here — use the text search there.

### MySQL / MariaDB — triggers and routines (M)

Sources: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/information-schema-triggers-table.html ·
https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/information-schema-routines-table.html

```sql
SELECT TRIGGER_NAME, ACTION_TIMING, EVENT_MANIPULATION FROM information_schema.TRIGGERS
WHERE TRIGGER_SCHEMA = DATABASE()
  AND (EVENT_OBJECT_TABLE = 'orders' OR ACTION_STATEMENT LIKE '%legacy_ref%');

SELECT ROUTINE_NAME, ROUTINE_TYPE FROM information_schema.ROUTINES
WHERE ROUTINE_SCHEMA = DATABASE() AND ROUTINE_DEFINITION LIKE '%legacy_ref%';
```

`ROUTINE_DEFINITION` visibility depends on the reader's privileges — the
ROUTINES page states the rule. An empty result under a restricted account is
not evidence of no dependents; say which account ran it.

## 3. Redundant indexes by leading-prefix relation

An index is redundant when its key columns are a leading prefix of another index
on the same table, with the same method, neither partial nor on an expression,
and the shorter one carries no uniqueness the longer one lacks.

### PostgreSQL — `pg_index` (M)

Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/catalog-pg-index.html

```sql
SELECT a.indexrelid::regclass AS redundant, b.indexrelid::regclass AS covered_by
FROM pg_index a
JOIN pg_index b ON b.indrelid = a.indrelid AND b.indexrelid <> a.indexrelid
JOIN pg_class ca ON ca.oid = a.indexrelid
JOIN pg_class cb ON cb.oid = b.indexrelid AND cb.relam = ca.relam
WHERE a.indrelid = 'public.orders'::regclass AND NOT a.indisunique
  AND ca.relam = (SELECT oid FROM pg_am WHERE amname = 'btree')  -- prefix logic is B-tree only
  AND a.indpred IS NULL AND b.indpred IS NULL        -- no partial indexes
  AND a.indexprs IS NULL AND b.indexprs IS NULL      -- no expression indexes
  AND (array_to_string((b.indkey::int2[])[0:b.indnkeyatts - 1], ' ') || ' ')
      LIKE (array_to_string((a.indkey::int2[])[0:a.indnkeyatts - 1], ' ') || ' %');
```

Only **key** columns are compared: `indkey` also lists `INCLUDE` columns after
the first `indnkeyatts` entries, and those do not take part in the prefix
relation. The trailing space stops `1 2` matching `1 23`. Identical pairs appear twice. Compare `indclass`
(operator classes) by hand before calling one redundant.

### MySQL — `STATISTICS`, or the `sys` view (H for the view)

`sys.schema_redundant_indexes` already does the prefix comparison and returns
`redundant_index_name`, `dominant_index_name` and `sql_drop_index`
(https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/sys-schema-redundant-indexes.html).
Read `sql_drop_index`; do not run it from the census. Where `sys` is absent,
list the key columns from `STATISTICS` and compare prefixes by eye
(https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/information-schema-statistics-table.html):

```sql
SELECT INDEX_NAME, NON_UNIQUE, GROUP_CONCAT(COLUMN_NAME ORDER BY SEQ_IN_INDEX) AS key_columns
FROM information_schema.STATISTICS
WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE() AND TABLE_NAME = 'orders'
GROUP BY INDEX_NAME, NON_UNIQUE;
```

### Unused indexes — referenced, not restated

The unused-index audit is row `Over-indexing writes` at
[`query-tuning.csv`](../data/query-tuning.csv) line 11 (`pg_stat_user_indexes
idx_scan = 0`). Use it as written.

## 4. Orphan rows — where the foreign key was never declared

§ 1 finds nothing for a relation the schema never declared. Probe the data
itself, per suspected relation (portable SQL, H):

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orphans
FROM order_items c LEFT JOIN orders p ON p.id = c.order_id
WHERE c.order_id IS NOT NULL AND p.id IS NULL;
```

Non-zero means adding the foreign key fails until the rows are fixed — a data
decision, not a migration step. On a large table run it on a replica.

## 5. Worked example — the view surfaces before the plan

Change under analysis: *drop column `orders.legacy_ref`* (PostgreSQL 17).

1. `blast-radius-analyzer` greps the repository: 2 call sites, 1 migration,
   0 views — the view was created by hand in production and is in no file.
2. § 2 view query, `refobjid = 'public.orders'`, `attname = 'legacy_ref'`:

   ```
    dependent_view          | relkind | column_used
   -------------------------+---------+-------------
    reporting.order_export  | v       | legacy_ref
   ```

3. The census output lists `reporting.order_export` as a consumer **before**
   any migration plan exists. Without it the plan is one `DROP COLUMN`, which
   PostgreSQL refuses while a view depends on the column unless `CASCADE` is
   given — and `CASCADE` drops the view
   (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-altertable.html). Either outcome would
   be found in production. The view goes into § 6 and gets its six answers.

## 6. Per-consumer compatibility questions

A consumer list does not constrain a migration; these answers do. Every consumer
from `blast-radius-analyzer` or §§ 1–4 gets all six. "Unknown" is valid and
becomes an open question; a blank is not.

| # | Question | Answer form |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Reads the old shape? | yes / no / unknown + evidence |
| Q2 | Writes the old shape? | yes / no / unknown + evidence |
| Q3 | Reads the new shape? | yes / no (not yet) / unknown |
| Q4 | Writes the new shape? | yes / no (not yet) / unknown |
| Q5 | Constrains rollout order? | must change before / after / independent |
| Q6 | Has a characterization test? | test file:line / none |

Template, one row per consumer:

| Consumer | Source | Q1 reads old | Q2 writes old | Q3 reads new | Q4 writes new | Q5 order | Q6 test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | | | | | | | |

### Worked example — two consumers, twelve answers

Change: replace `orders.legacy_ref` (text) with `orders.external_ref_id` (FK to
`external_refs`).

| Consumer | Source | Q1 reads old | Q2 writes old | Q3 reads new | Q4 writes new | Q5 order | Q6 test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reporting.order_export` (view) | § 2 catalog query | yes — selects `legacy_ref` | no — views do not write here | no | no | must be redefined before the old column is dropped | none |
| `OrderSyncJob` | blast-radius call site | yes | yes — sets it on import | no (not yet) | no (not yet) | must dual-write before readers switch; old writes stop last | the job's test file (file:line from grep) |

Twelve answers, and they order the work: the job dual-writes before anything
reads the new column, the view moves before the drop, and the missing view test
is an output — characterize `order_export` before changing it.

## Hand-off

The table from § 6 is the input to
[`migration-architect`](../../migration-architect/SKILL.md)'s phase sequencing:
Q2/Q4 decide whether a dual-write phase exists, Q1/Q3 decide when readers switch,
Q5 orders the phases, and every `none` in Q6 is a test that lands before its
phase. The census reports; it does not plan, and it does not execute a drop.
